is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (predominantly Anopheles coluzzii, plus An. melas and An. gambiae s.s.) as well as An. pharoensis and An. ziemanni (page 2, section 2.2; page 3, section 3.1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Screened for 'The knock-down resistance mutation (kdr-west, L1014F) and acetylcholinesterase resistance mutation (Ace1)... detected by Taqman allelic discrimination assays as described by Bass (Bass et al., 2007)' (page 2, section 2.3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table III (page 3) provides exact kdr (L1014F) genotype counts: Flood (RR=90, RS=38, SS=8), Fall (RR=309, RS=248, SS=7), Total (RR=399, RS=286, SS=15). Page 3, section 3.4 states: 'Concerning ace1 gene, only one Anopheles coluzzii of the 770 Anopheles gambiae s.l. tested successfully was heterozygote for the mutation'.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Sô-Ava District, southern Benin, between July 2014 and June 2015 using CDC light traps and larval collections (page 2, section 2.1-2.2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical field study reporting mosquito diversity, CSP infection rates, WHO bioassay susceptibility, and genotype data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Sô-Ava District (6° 28′ 00″ N, 2° 25′ 00″ E), Atlantic Department, southern Benin (page 2, section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Surveys were conducted between July 2014 and June 2015 (page 2, section 2.2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard entomological field survey conducted by local university/CREC/IRD researchers without indication of being part of a larger consortium or re-used dataset.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts and frequencies are reported directly in the main text and Table III.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated mosquito diversity, Plasmodium falciparum CSP infection rates, and insecticide resistance in Sô-Ava District, a lagoon area in southern Benin between July 2014 and June 2015. Genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and Ace-1 G280S was performed on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (largely An. coluzzii), providing full RR/RS/SS counts. WHO susceptibility bioassays were conducted with several pyrethroids, organophosphates, DDT, and bendiocarb.
